sources.entry: HitKeep - Privacy-first web analytics with goals, funnels, ecommerce tracking, and team management in a single binary with embedded DuckDB (alternative to Google Analytics, Plausible, Umami). (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: HitKeep is a self-hostable, MIT-licensed web analytics platform shipped as a single Go binary with embedded DuckDB, covering traffic, goals, funnels, ecommerce, Search Console, and AI-referred visits.
summary.what_it_does: HitKeep provides web analytics for websites, delivered as one Go binary with embedded DuckDB and NSQ, so no separate database, queue, or cache is needed. A browser tracker script records pageviews plus automatic events such as outbound clicks, file downloads, and form submissions, and supports custom events for actions like signups or purchases. Reporting covers acquisition through pages, goals, funnels, ecommerce revenue, UTM and QR campaigns, Search Console data, and Web Vitals. It separates AI traffic (crawler fetches, AI-referred visits, chatbot outcomes) from other traffic, offers an "Ask AI" feature that answers from cited aggregate data, and includes a read-only MCP interface for approved assistants. Team features include SSO, custom tracking domains, share links, permissions, and open-format exports, APIs, and webhooks. The tracker sets no analytics cookies and respects Do Not Track.
use_cases: replace Google Analytics with a privacy-focused tool
track conversions and funnels on a website
monitor AI chatbot and crawler traffic
share analytics with a team using SSO and permissions
how_to_run: Download compose.yml and .env template from the repository (URLs not preserved in README)
Replace 'paste-the-generated-value-here' in .env with a long random secret
notable: Single binary with embedded DuckDB and NSQ; no separate database, queue, or cache required
AI-native analytics: distinguishes crawler fetches, AI-referred visits, and chatbot outcomes; read-only MCP access for assistants
Custom tracking domains and team SSO included in the MIT-licensed public codebase
Open data export formats, complete takeout, APIs, and webhooks
caveats: Web-focused: no session replay, mobile SDKs, or built-in experimentation
Homebrew install covers Apple silicon macOS and x86_64 Linux; Linux ARM64 requires the binary or Docker
DuckDB extensions are extracted to HITKEEP_DATA_PATH/.duckdb/extensions, which must be writable and not mounted noexec
